facts.statement: Omeisaurus was named after Mount Emei in Sichuan Province, China, where fossils were found in the lower Shaximiao Formation.
facts.quote: Its name comes from Mount Emei, where it was discovered in the lower Shaximiao Formation of Sichuan Province.

facts.statement: Omeisaurus lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic Period (Bathonian to Oxfordian stages) in what is now China.
facts.quote: Omeisaurus (meaning "Omei lizard") is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Middle to Late Jurassic Period (Bathonian-Oxfordian stage) of what is now China.

facts.statement: The largest species, O. tianfuensis, reached lengths of 18 to 20.2 meters and weighed between 8.5 and 9.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: The largest species, O. tianfuensis, measured 18 - 20.2 m long, and weighed 8.5 - 9.8 MT.

facts.statement: The first Omeisaurus fossils were collected in 1936 by Charles Lewis Camp and Yang Zhongjian from the Shaximiao Formation in Sichuan.
facts.quote: The initial discovery of Omeisaurus was in 1936 when Charles Lewis Camp and Yang Zhongjian collected a partial skeleton from strata of the Shaximiao Formation in Sichuan, China.

facts.statement: The original skeleton of the type species O. junghsiensis was lost during World War II.
facts.quote: The skeleton of O. junghsiensis was lost during WWII.

facts.statement: A vast amount of Omeisaurus material was discovered in the 1970s during the construction of the Wujiaba Dam in Zigong.
facts.quote: During the construction of the Wujiaba Dam in Zigong during the mid-to-late 1970s, crews discovered many large Sauropod remains from strata of the Upper Shaximiao Formation.

facts.statement: The species O. fuxiensis was described in 1983 based on a fragmentary partial skull found at the Wujiaba site.
facts.quote: Wujiaba also saw the collection of a fragmentary partial skull of an additional species of Omeisaurus, Omeisaurus fuxiensis, that was described by Zhiming Dong and colleagues in 1983.

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton (ZDM T5701) found at Dashanpu was designated the holotype for O. tianfuensis and described in 1984.
facts.quote: The best of these skeletons, a nearly complete and semi articulated postcranial skeleton (ZDM T5701), was selected as the holotype and described by He et al in 1984.

facts.statement: A specimen from Dashanpu revealed that O. tianfuensis possessed a tail club formed by modified caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Interestingly, O. tianfuensis was discovered to have a tail club on the end of its caudal vertebrae based on a specimen from Dashanpu.

facts.statement: O. puxiani, discovered in Yunyang, is one of the best-preserved species with fossils including most of the vertebral column and girdles.
facts.quote: The most recently named Omeisaurus species, O. puxiani, was discovered in Yunyang and is one of the best preserved Omeisaurus species, with fossils from most of the vertebral column and girdles recovered.

facts.statement: Omeisaurus was formerly classified in Euhelopodidae but is now placed in the family Mamenchisauridae, a more basal sauropod group.
facts.quote: Omeisaurus was formerly assigned to Euhelopodidae. However, it and other Jurassic sauropods from Asia formerly assigned to Euhelopodidae are now placed in the separate family Mamenchisauridae, which is more basal in Sauropoda.

facts.statement: A 2021 study by John D'Angelo validated most Omeisaurus species as members of the same genus, excluding O. maoianus.
facts.quote: In 2021, John D'Angelo determined that all Omeisaurus species, besides O. maoianus, were valid and likely members of the same genus, with O. junghsiensis as the most basal species.

facts.statement: Omeisaurus possessed 17 cervical vertebrae, which is more than the average number found in medium-sized sauropods.
facts.quote: Omeisaurus no sólo tiene un cuello largo, también tenía varias vértebras cervicales más que los saurópodos medios, con un total de 17.

facts.statement: The species O. tianfuensis had the longest neck in the genus, measuring approximately 9 meters.
facts.quote: O. tianfuensis tenía el cuello más largo del género, alrededor de 9 metros de largo.

facts.statement: O. fuxiensis was the smallest species in the genus, reaching a length of about 11 meters.
facts.quote: O. fuxiensis fue la especie más pequeña, midiendo alrededor de 11 metros.

facts.statement: Omeisaurus had a wedge-shaped skull with about 60 chisel-like, non-edged teeth adapted for stripping vegetation.
facts.quote: Su cráneo tenía forma de cuña, con unos 60 dientes biselados sin filos, ideales para arrancar la vegetación de la que se alimentaba.

facts.statement: Unlike most sauropods, Omeisaurus had nostrils located near the tip of its snout.
facts.quote: Las fosas nasales se encontraban, a diferencia de la mayoría de los saurópodos, cerca del final del morro.

facts.statement: Large herds of Omeisaurus likely roamed alongside stegosaurs like Tuojiangosaurus and Chungkingosaurus, making it one of the most common sauropods in Jurassic China.
facts.quote: Las grandes manadas de Omeisaurus vagaron probablemente, junto a los estegosáuridos como Tuojiangosaurus y Chungkingosaurus, siendo probablemente uno de los saurópodos más comunes de su época en China.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the tail club found in the same fossil beds as Omeisaurus actually belongs to Omeisaurus or to a large Shunosaurus.
facts.quote: La porra de la cola encontrada en el mismo lecho de fósiles que Omeisaurus y que se había asignado a este género, hoy se piensa que podría pertenecer a un Shunosaurus muy grande.

facts.statement: The classification of O. maoianus is debated, with some analyses suggesting it is more closely related to Mamenchisaurus and Xinjiangtitan than to other Omeisaurus species.
facts.quote: O. maoianus generic assessment has been questioned, with several phylogenetic analyses finding it more closely related to Mamenchisaurus and Xinjiangtitan.

facts.statement: Omeisaurus lived during the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian to Tithonian stages), approximately 163 to 145 million years ago, in Asia.
facts.quote: Omeisaurus ("lagarto de Omei") es un género de dinosaurios saurópodos eusaurópodos que vivieron a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 163 a 145 millones de años, desde el Oxfordiense y el Tithoniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Omeisaurus inhabited dense forests, and different species sometimes shared the same habitats.
facts.quote: Omeisaurus lived in dense forests. Different species of Omeisaurus sometimes shared habitats with each other (O. junghsiensis and O. tianfuensis, for example).

facts.statement: The first fossil specimen of Omeisaurus was found in the Xiashaximiao Formation in Sichuan, China, in 1939.
facts.quote: El primer espécimen fósil de esta especie fue encontrado en la Formación Xiashaximiao en Sichuan, China en 1939

facts.statement: The species was described by Yang Zhongjian, known as Chung Chien Young in the West.
facts.quote: y descrito por Yang Zhongjian conocido como Chung Chien Young en Occidente

facts.statement: The name Omeisaurus comes from the place where it was discovered, Mount Emei.
facts.quote: El nombre proviene del lugar donde fuera descubierto, el Monte Emei u Omeshian

facts.statement: Most Omeisaurus skeletons were found between the years 1970 and 1980.
facts.quote: La mayoría de los esqueletos de Omeisaurus fueron encontrados entre los años de 1970 y 1980

facts.statement: At least 8 species of Omeisaurus have been named so far.
facts.quote: Se conocen por lo menos 8 especies de Omeisaurus nombradas hasta ahora

facts.statement: Omeisaurus fuxiensis is sometimes confused with Zigongosaurus.
facts.quote: Omeisaurus fuxiensis es confundida a veces con Zigongosaurus

facts.statement: Mounted skeletons of Omeisaurus are exhibited at the Zigong Dinosaur Museum in Sichuan Province and the Beipei Museum near Chongqing.
facts.quote: Esqueletos montados de Omeisaurus se encuentran exhibidos en el Museo de Dinosaurios de Zigong, Provincia de Sichuan y en el Museo Beipei cerca de Chongqing

facts.statement: Omeisaurus was initially placed within the family Cetiosauridae.
facts.quote: Omeisaurus fue colocado en un principio dentro de la familia Cetiosauridae

facts.statement: Currently, Omeisaurus lacks a family and is considered a eusauropod.
facts.quote: Actualmente carece de familia y se lo considera como un eusaurópodo

facts.statement: Omeisaurus and other Jurassic Asian sauropods previously assigned to Euhelopodidae are now located in the separate family Mamenchisauridae.
facts.quote: él y otros saurópodos jurásicos de Asia anteriormente asignados a Euhelopodidae ahora se ubican en la familia separada Mamenchisauridae

facts.statement: The parent group of Omeisaurus is Mamenchisauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Mamenchisauridae

facts.statement: Omeisaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Omeisaurus lived from the Aalenian to the Tithonian stages, between 174.7 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aalenian to Tithonian (174.7 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2026 study by Kubo et al. found no evidence of significant differences in tooth microwear texture in an Omeisaurus maoianus specimen based on tooth position.
facts.quote: Kubo et al. (2026) study tooth wear of a specimen of Omeisaurus maoianus, finding no evidence of significant differences of microwear texture in the same individual based on tooth position

facts.statement: It is debated regarding the phylogenetic relationships of Omeisaurus species, with Xing et al. (2015) and Ren et al. (2018) suggesting O. maoianus is more closely related to Mamenchisaurus than to O. tianfuensis.
facts.quote: En su artículo sobre Qijianglong , Xing et al. en 2015 consideraron a O. maoianus más estrechamente relacionado con Mamenchisaurus que a O. tianfuensis, una propuesta apoyada por el análisis cladistico de Ren et al. en 2018
